title: The journey of food
summary: Review how the digestive system works and how our body uses nutrients.
keyIdeas: Digestion breaks down food to obtain the nutrients we need.
The digestive tract starts at the mouth and ends at the anus.
Most nutrients pass into the blood through the small intestine.

basicKnowledge: A. Cultura científica › Iniciación en la actividad científica
A. Cultura científica › La vida en nuestro planeta

activities.prompt: Lucía eats an apple at break time. Where does digestion of this food begin? 🍎
activities.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth, where teeth break up food and saliva moistens it.
activities.hint: It is where we chew food.

activities.prompt: The oesophagus is a tube connecting the mouth directly to the small intestine.
activities.explanation: The oesophagus connects the throat to the stomach, rather than to the small intestine.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about digestion with the right word.
activities.explanation: Gastric juices in the stomach help break down food into a soft mixture.
activities.hint: The word begins with g and relates to the stomach.
activities.sentence: In the stomach, food mixes with ___ juices to help break it down.

activities.prompt: Put the route of a piece of bread through the digestive tract in order.
activities.explanation: Food passes from the mouth through the oesophagus, stomach, small intestine and finally the large intestine.

activities.prompt: Match each part of the digestive system to its main job.
activities.explanation: Teeth chew food, the small intestine absorbs nutrients, and the large intestine absorbs water from the remaining material.

activities.prompt: Sort these body parts into organs of the digestive tract or glands that help digestion.
activities.explanation: The digestive tract is the hollow route food travels through. The liver, pancreas and salivary glands make substances that help digestion.

activities.prompt: Read about Omar's experience and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Chemical digestion begins in the mouth because saliva contains substances that break down food.
activities.title: The cracker experiment
activities.text: Omar learns about digestion in science class. The teacher explains what happens when we chew a savoury cracker. At first, it tastes salty and feels crunchy. Slowly, saliva soaks into it. Omar notices something curious: after chewing for a while, the cracker starts to taste a little sweet. The teacher explains that saliva contains special substances called enzymes. They break down complex carbohydrates in the cracker into simpler sugars.

questions.prompt: Which liquid in the mouth changes the cracker during the experiment?
questions.explanation: The text explains that saliva acts on the cracker.

questions.prompt: Why does the cracker start to taste sweet?
questions.explanation: Enzymes in saliva break down the starch in bread or crackers into simpler sugars.
options: Saliva breaks down carbohydrates into simpler sugars

activities.prompt: Think scientifically: Martina eats very quickly and hardly chews. What might happen in her stomach? 🧪
activities.explanation: Chewing well makes food pieces smaller and mixes them with saliva. This helps the digestive system do its work.
activities.hint: Think about the extra work the stomach will need to do.
options: Large pieces could make digestion harder
Nutrients will enter the blood instantly
The stomach will digest everything faster because there is no saliva

activities.prompt: Find the mistake: Hugo writes three statements in his notebook. Which one is incorrect? ❌
activities.explanation: Most nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine. The large intestine mainly absorbs water and forms faeces.
options: Faeces leave the body through the anus
Chewed food and saliva form a ball of food in the mouth
The large intestine absorbs most of the nutrients that enter the blood

activities.prompt: Drinking enough water and eating foods with fibre help the intestine work properly.
activities.explanation: Water and fibre help material move through the digestive tract and help prevent constipation.
